canonical.definition: The engineering of the scaffold around a model — loop, prompts, tools, memory, and control flow — treated as the primary unit of design and iteration, distinct from the model itself.
The practice of deciding what information enters a model's context and in what form, treating context assembly as a first-class engineering discipline rather than prompt wording.
Techniques for shrinking accumulated context — summarizing, trimming, or rewriting history — so an agent can keep running past what would otherwise be a full window.
Budgeting and allocating a finite context window across system prompt, tools, history, and retrieved material, including policies for what gets evicted when the budget is exceeded.
Packaged, model-invocable units of procedural knowledge (instructions plus optional resources) that extend an agent's capabilities without retraining or hard-coding.
Models exploiting the measurable proxy — reward function, grader, test suite, or eval — instead of solving the intended task, and the detection of that behavior.
Using a language model to grade or compare outputs, including its calibration against human labels and its known failure modes as an evaluator.
aliases: judge validation with precision and recall

canonical.definition: Constructing the task environments agents are trained in — task distribution, difficulty, tooling surface, and termination — as the main lever on learned behavior.
Post-training on tasks whose success can be checked programmatically (tests, compilers, solvers) rather than by a learned preference model.
Building the checker that decides whether an agent's output is correct — its coverage, strictness, cost, and resistance to being gamed — whether used for training or gating.
Coordinating several agents as a system — topology, handoffs, shared state, and consensus — as opposed to one agent calling tools.
A parent agent spawning scoped child agents to isolate context and specialize work, then folding their results back into its own trajectory.
MCP as a protocol and ecosystem for connecting models to tools, resources, and applications — its primitives, adoption, and role as a standard.
Requiring explicit human authorization before an agent takes a consequential or irreversible action, including how approval is scoped and where gates are placed.
Persisting and recalling information across an agent's turns, sessions, or lifetime — storage substrate, write policy, and retrieval policy.
The machinery that runs evaluations — task definition, execution, scoring, reproducibility, and CI integration — as opposed to what is being measured.
Constructing a benchmark that measures what it claims to — task selection, difficulty calibration, discrimination, and holdout discipline.
Instrumenting agent runs so every step, tool call, and token is inspectable after the fact — spans, traces, and the tooling that renders them.
Untrusted content in an agent's context hijacking its instructions, and the mitigations for it; covers both the attack and the defenses.
Confining agent execution — filesystem, network, syscalls, process — so that a misbehaving or compromised agent cannot affect the host or production systems.
Engineers embedded with customers to build, tune, and ship AI systems in the customer's environment, and the operating model that makes that repeatable.
Systems that keep improving after deployment by incorporating new experience — through weights, memory, or artifacts — rather than being frozen at training time.
Dispatching requests to different models by task difficulty, cost, or capability, including fallback chains and gateway layers.
How engineers actually work with coding agents day to day — delegation patterns, review rhythm, parallelism, and the shape of the resulting dev loop.
Writing an explicit specification as the durable artifact that agents implement against, making the spec rather than the code the primary human authored input.
Agents that operate GUIs, browsers, and screens directly — grounding on pixels, DOM, or accessibility trees — rather than through purpose-built APIs.
Grounding generation in an external corpus retrieved at inference time; the overall architecture, not any single retrieval component.
Building and maintaining an explicit graph of entities and relations as a substrate for agent reasoning, retrieval, or enterprise context.
Reducing tokens spent per unit of useful work — trimming tool schemas, prompts, and outputs — treated as a design constraint on agent architecture.
Work that spans many steps, hours, or days, where the difficulty comes from horizon length — accumulated error, state, and coherence — not per-step difficulty.
Agents that modify their own prompts, skills, tools, or harness based on their results, closing a loop from outcome back to configuration.
The structure of the perceive–decide–act–observe cycle itself: iteration control, stopping conditions, and how control flows between model and runtime.
Designing the tool surface an agent sees — naming, granularity, schemas, and affordances — so the model can use it reliably.
aliases: typed sdk as constrained action surface

canonical.definition: Model-generated training, fine-tuning, or evaluation data, including quality control and the risks of training on generated distributions.
Using models or agents to review diffs and pull requests — reviewer agents, review personas, and where automated review fits in the pipeline.
Harvesting real production agent transcripts as the raw material for evals, training data, and failure discovery.
Making agents fail rarely and recover gracefully — error compounding across steps, retries, degradation, and reliability as a system property.
Loading instructions, tools, or reference material into context only when needed, keeping the default context small and expanding it on demand.
Degradation of model behavior as context grows or ages — attention dilution, stale facts, and instruction drift over long conversations.
Benchmarks losing signal as scores approach ceiling or as the field optimizes directly against them, and the resulting short half-life of evals.
Evaluation data leaking into training corpora, and the detection, decontamination, and holdout practices that address it.
Pre-deployment evaluation against fixed datasets and splits, run before shipping rather than against live traffic.
Measuring quality against live production traffic — monitoring, experiments, and implicit user signals — rather than a static dataset.
Writing the scoring criteria that graders — human or model — apply, including criterion drift and inter-grader consistency.
Scoring the whole path an agent took — steps, tool calls, and recovery — rather than only its final answer.
Systematically clustering observed failures into named modes so effort can be aimed at the largest buckets.
aliases: error analysis and failure mode clustering
root cause analysis for agent failures

canonical.definition: Treating evals as the development loop — writing them first, hill-climbing against them, and gating releases on them.
aliases: evals in ci as release gates

canonical.definition: Sourcing and calibrating human judgments used as ground truth — annotator agreement, expert labeling, and alignment of judges to human labels.
Benchmarks specifically for software-engineering agents — task realism, repo grounding, and what SWE-style scores do and don't predict.
Synthetic or cloned environments used to exercise agents safely at scale, including simulated users and the gap between simulation and reality.
Evaluating work with no programmatic ground truth — taste, judgment, and expert-domain quality — where verifiable rewards do not apply.
Measuring the retrieval stage on its own terms — recall, precision, and corpus freshness — separately from end-to-end answer quality.
Transferring capability from a larger or stronger teacher model into a smaller student, including on-policy and reasoning-trace variants.
The stage after pre-training — SFT, RL, and mid-training — where task behavior is shaped, treated as its own engineering pipeline.
Selecting, mixing, filtering, and sequencing training corpora, and the ablations used to attribute capability to data choices.
Predictable relationships between compute, data, parameters, and capability, and how compute is allocated across the training stack.
aliases: compute allocation across the training stack
compute allocation between pre-training and post-training

canonical.definition: Reducing numeric precision of weights or activations to cut memory and cost, and the quality tradeoffs that come with it.
Running models on the user's own hardware — laptop, phone, edge device, or self-hosted server — instead of a hosted API.
Deliberately small or narrowly specialized models chosen for cost, latency, or deployability over frontier generality.
Managing the unit economics of serving models — cost per token, per query, and per agent run — as a first-order product constraint.
Exploiting and managing the KV cache — prefix reuse, compression, cache-aware serving — to cut latency and cost.
Allocating an end-to-end response-time budget across model calls and system hops, including tail latency and time-to-first-token targets.
Spending more compute at inference — longer reasoning, sampling, or search — to buy accuracy without changing weights.
Loss of prior capability when a model is updated on new data, and the stability–plasticity tradeoff that governs it.
Training on human preference signals — pairwise comparisons, reward models, and the asymmetries they introduce.
Shaping the reward signal itself — density, sparsity, and credit assignment across long rollouts — as distinct from designing the environment or the verifier.
Authoring the instruction text itself — system prompts, examples, role framing — and the limits of what wording alone can fix.
Automated search over prompts against a metric, replacing hand-tuning with an optimizer.
Constraining model output to a schema or type so downstream systems can consume it deterministically.
Runtime checks on model input and output that block, filter, or rewrite unacceptable content before it reaches users or systems.
Reducing confident fabrication and sycophancy, and calibrating how much trust an output's confidence deserves.
Tying generated claims back to specific sources so a reader can verify provenance, including attribution and evidence traceability.
A governed modeling layer over business data that gives metrics and entities canonical definitions models can query without inventing joins.
Defining the entity types and relationships of a domain as an explicit schema that agents and graphs are built on.
Deciding when records across sources refer to the same real-world thing, and merging them without collapsing distinct entities.
Retrieval that traverses a knowledge graph — communities, paths, subgraphs — instead of or alongside flat vector lookup.
Combining dense vector search with lexical or structured search and fusing the result sets.
The mechanics between corpus and context — chunking, indexing, reranking, and top-k thresholds — as engineering choices with measurable effects.
Letting the model plan and iterate its own searches — issuing queries, reading results, and re-querying — instead of a fixed one-shot retrieval step.
Acquiring and representing web-scale content for models — crawling, scraping, anti-bot handling, and page-to-token representation.
Turning PDFs, scans, and other unstructured documents into structured text a model can consume, including layout and table extraction.
Models that reason jointly over images and text, and applications built on visual understanding rather than text alone.
Real-time speech-driven agents and the pipeline concerns unique to them — turn taking, barge-in, endpointing, and conversational latency.
Interfaces the model generates or drives at runtime — rendered components, ephemeral views, server-driven layouts — rather than fixed screens.
Designing how people perceive, steer, and collaborate with AI systems — progress disclosure, steering affordances, and trust-shaping UX.
Explicit gradations of how much an agent may decide and act unsupervised, and how systems move up or down that ladder.
Human oversight degrading because reviewers rubber-stamp agent output — approval fatigue, alert fatigue, and the erosion of meaningful review.
Routing to a human when the agent is uncertain or the stakes are high, based on confidence or risk rather than a blanket approval rule.
Giving agents their own principals, credentials, and delegated authority so their actions are attributable and scoped to a user's grant.
Restricting which tools, data, and credentials an agent can reach to the minimum its task requires, and keeping secrets out of its context.
Risk entering through dependencies, packages, models, and third-party skills or servers, including AI-specific vectors like hallucinated package names.
A layer that evaluates and enforces rules on agent actions as they execute, independent of what the model was asked to do.
Durable, attributable records of what an agent did and why, produced for compliance and after-the-fact accountability rather than debugging.
Organizational and regulatory control over AI systems — policy, approval, disclosure, and demonstrating conformance to auditors.
Running models under jurisdictional or network isolation — on-prem, VPC, air-gapped, or nationally controlled — and the geopolitics that drive it.
Controlling what data may enter model context and where it may flow — PII handling, redaction, residency, lineage, and ownership.
Using models and agents to find, verify, and triage security vulnerabilities in code or running systems.
Preventing agents from writing insecure code, and the static analysis and CI gates that catch it when they do.
Open protocols letting agents, clients, and services from different vendors talk to each other, and the open-versus-walled-garden dynamics around them.
Building and operating MCP servers well — tool surface, resource modeling, statefulness, and server-side security posture.
Distribution and governance of agent extensions — registries, app stores, vetting, and internal catalogs.
Agents that run detached from a live session — scheduled, event-triggered, or long-lived — and notify rather than being watched.
The compute substrate agents run on — VM and container pools, warm starts, cloud dev environments — as an operations and cost problem distinct from security isolation.
Running many agents or branches concurrently and merging their results, including workspace isolation and fan-out/fan-in patterns.
Breaking a large goal into scoped, independently checkable units sized to what an agent can actually complete.
Runtimes that survive crashes and restarts by persisting agent state — checkpointing, replay, and idempotent resumption of long-running work.
The lifecycle of an agent session as a portable object — persisting, resuming, forking, and sharing it across clients or users.
Keeping a system swappable across models, harnesses, and vendors so no single provider becomes structurally load-bearing.
Deciding whether to build an AI capability in-house or adopt a vendor's, and when a thin wrapper stops being enough.
Measuring whether AI tooling actually made engineering faster or better — velocity, delivery, and adoption instrumentation.
Getting an organization to actually work differently with AI — enablement, champions, process redesign, and the org shapes that result.
Human review becoming the constraint once agents generate code faster than people can read it, and how teams restructure review to cope.
Whether agent-written code is maintainable and correct beyond passing tests — slop, accumulated debt, and unverified output.
Erosion of human understanding, skill, and ownership as work shifts to agents — the human-side cost of delegation.
aliases: human taste and judgment in agentic workflows

canonical.definition: Selling and distributing AI products — positioning, ICP, sales motion, pricing models, and developer-led distribution.
Quantifying the business return of AI deployments and using it to prioritize, justify, or kill agent investments.
Extracting what should actually be built from stakeholders and turning it into a scoped, checkable statement of work.
Product usage generating proprietary data that improves the product, compounding into a durable advantage.
Inspecting model internals — features, activations, circuits — to explain or steer behavior, as opposed to black-box evaluation.
Learned internal or simulated models of an environment that a system can plan or generate against.
Agents running the scientific loop — hypothesis generation, experiment design, analysis — in research and biomedical domains.
Handling inputs far larger than a normal window — long-context architectures, sparse attention, and recursive decomposition over the input.
Restructuring a repository and its documentation so agents can navigate and change it — the codebase as an interface for models.
Making a codebase queryable for agents — indexing, symbol and call graphs, and cross-repo search that feeds context.
Using agents to modernize, refactor, or port existing systems at a scale that was previously not worth the human cost.
Deciding which parts of a system must be deterministic code and which can be model-driven, and how to layer the two.
Using a second model or agent with independent context to check the first's work, including writer/reviewer separation and multi-model consensus.
aliases: separation of writer and reviewer agents

canonical.definition: Dedicated monitor agents that watch another agent for misbehavior, drift, or sabotage, rather than for output quality.
The model picking the right tool from a catalog, and the accuracy and discovery problems that appear as catalogs grow.
Checked-in files that persistently steer an agent's behavior — rules, instructions, and voice — as versioned artifacts a team edits together.
Agents in the operational loop — triaging alerts, investigating root cause, and remediating production issues.
aliases: incident triage and root cause investigation

canonical.definition: Turning tacit organizational and team knowledge into durable, retrievable artifacts that agents and people can both use.
Production pipelines that generate video, slides, or other rich media from code or prompts, including how such output is evaluated.
Agents built for a specific regulated or specialized industry, where domain workflow and expertise dominate the design.

drop_guidance: Drop single-talk implementation trivia that names a specific mechanism inside one system rather than a reusable idea: 'chrome devtools protocol', 'durable objects', 'block-level snapshotting', 'prefix tokenization at write time', 'micro-block scaled number formats', 'chat template tokenization', 'sarif reporting'. If the surrounding idea is covered, map to the parent (e.g. 'copy-on-write storage' → agent execution infrastructure); otherwise drop.

Drop generic software-engineering and infrastructure patterns with no AI-specific angle and no cross-talk presence: 'composition over inheritance', 'free monads', 'partial function application', 'database sharding', 'read/write splitting across replicas', 'horizontal pod autoscaling', 'lambda architecture', 'backend for frontend', 'decoupled microservices'. These are incidental architecture mentions, not conference concepts.

Drop talk-craft, rhetoric, and presentation framing: 'before-and-after framing', 'analogy-based explanation', 'thinking in public', 'pitch narrative structure', 'go-to-market storytelling', 'elevator pitch', 'jargon reduction', 'leading words', 'xy problem', 'napkin math estimation'. These describe how a talk was delivered, not what it was about.

Drop narrow domain-science and vertical minutiae that only one talk could ever engage: 'rna sequencing', 'spatial transcriptomics', 'cellular reprogramming', 'medical image translation', 'image registration', 'gaze estimation', 'clinical knowledge graph', 'payer rule knowledge base'. Where the talk's AI-facing point survives, map it to agentic science or vertical domain agents instead.

Drop one-off business and sales metrics that are not AI-engineering concepts: 'average contract value', 'buying committee detection', 'icp scoring', 'multi-touch attribution', 'cohort analysis', 'business model canvas', 'venture capital strategy', 'visitor de-anonymization'. Keep only what maps to go-to-market for ai products or roi measurement.

Drop statistical and psychometric method names used once with no currency across the conference: 'conditional average treatment effect', 'latent confounders', 'classical test theory', 'residual analysis', 'covariate shift', 'query by committee', 'confidence interval coverage'. Exceptions: 'item response theory', 'item difficulty calibration', and 'item discrimination' map to benchmark design, since benchmark rigor is a recurring theme.

Drop strings that are one talk's self-description rather than a concept — anything phrased as a case, result, or company-specific process. If a string only makes sense with the talk's context restored, it is tail; fold it into the nearest canonical parent or drop it.
notes: Deliberate separations. (1) 'context engineering' (what goes in), 'context window management' (budget allocation), 'context compaction' (shrinking what's there), 'context rot' (degradation), and 'long-context processing' (architectures for oversized inputs) are five distinct pages — do not collapse on the word 'context'. (2) 'rl environment design' (the task world), 'reward design' (the signal), 'verifier design' (the checker), and 'reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards' (the training regime) are separate; a talk about building graders goes to verifier design even if it says 'RL'. (3) 'human-in-the-loop approval' (pre-action authorization), 'human-in-the-loop escalation' (uncertainty/risk routing), and 'automation bias' (oversight failing) are three ideas; 'human-in-the-loop review'/'human review artifacts' map to approval; 'human-in-the-loop steering'/'runtime steering' map to human-ai interaction design. (4) 'agent sandboxing' is the security boundary; 'agent execution infrastructure' is the compute substrate (warm pools, micro VMs, cloud dev envs). Sandbox strings that emphasize isolation go to the former, capacity/ops strings to the latter. (5) 'cross-model verification' (a second model checks quality) is separate from 'adversarial agent supervision' (a monitor watches for misbehavior) — route by whether the concern is correctness or safety. (6) 'model context protocol' is the protocol/ecosystem page; 'mcp server design' is for talks about building or securing servers. A passing MCP mention goes to the former. (7) 'offline evaluation' and 'online evaluation' stay split — the offline/online boundary is a real methodological divide here. Deliberate merges. 'harness engineering', 'agentic harness design', 'meta harness design' and every 'agent harness *' variant collapse into one 'agent harness design' page — this was the largest lexical-variant family in the raw list. 'manager-worker agent architecture', 'supervisor-agent orchestration' and 'hierarchical multi-agent systems' fold into 'multi-agent orchestration'; only 'sub-agent delegation' survives separately because sub-agents are used for context isolation, not just topology. 'vendor lock-in' folds into 'model portability'. 'event sourcing', 'state machine orchestration', and checkpointing strings fold into 'durable execution'. 'semantic chunking' and 'reranking' merged into 'retrieval pipeline design'; 'hybrid retrieval' and 'graph rag' stayed separate because they name genuinely different retrieval architectures. Ambiguous boundaries the assignment pass should watch. 'agentic coding workflows' vs 'agent harness design': if the talk is about the tool's internals, use harness; if about how humans use it, use workflows. 'reward hacking' vs 'benchmark saturation': model exploiting a grader → reward hacking; the field over-optimizing a public benchmark → saturation. 'token efficiency' vs 'inference cost optimization': token counts as a context/design constraint → token efficiency; dollars and unit economics → inference cost. 'agent memory' vs 'institutional knowledge capture': agent-scoped state → memory; org-scoped shared knowledge → institutional knowledge. Many 'agent observability *' strings shade into 'production trace mining' — instrumentation and inspection → observability; using traces as eval/training input → trace mining. Multi-mapping is expected and fine: a raw string like 'skill and mcp server risk assessment' plausibly touches agent skills, mcp server design, and software supply chain security.
